I am 64 and have farmed a long time, so I will keep to a steady, practical way of farming instead of taking risks. Because I have well irrigation, I will use water at the key stages rather than depend only on rain. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put in moderate fertilizer, irrigate a few times, and do rotary tillage because it is familiar and manageable for me. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because I want stable yield in summer, keep fertilizer a bit higher on nitrogen, irrigate when needed, and continue with rotary tillage after the wheat season so the work is simpler. I will control pests with a limited number of sprays, only enough to protect yield and avoid unnecessary cost. My goal this year is stable production, manageable fieldwork, and reliable grain yield from both crops on the same land.
